9.concern: Minor: the blanket 'no BP cuffs/venipuncture on that arm' rule is traditional nursing teaching and is what the module states, but modern breast-surgery data (e.g. AMAROS/ASBrS-era studies) have not shown ipsilateral BP cuffs or venipuncture to raise lymphedema risk. Answer is still the intended and only defensible option.

5.concern: Mechanistic error in the keyed option as written: an antiandrogen does NOT prevent the initial testosterone surge — the surge still occurs; the antiandrogen blocks the androgen receptor so the surge has no clinical (tumor-flare) effect. Option A says 'to prevent the initial testosterone flare', which teaches the wrong mechanism. Only a GnRH ANTAGONIST (degarelix/relugolix) prevents the surge. Recommend rewording to 'to block the clinical tumor flare caused by the initial testosterone surge'. A is still the only defensible choice.

8.concern: The clause 'LMWH is preferred over warfarin' is true but now dated as a stand-alone statement — ASCO/ITAC/CHEST currently place apixaban/rivaroxaban/edoxaban alongside LMWH as first-line for cancer-associated VTE (LMWH still favored in luminal GI/unresected GI primaries, which does apply to pancreatic cancer). Consider adding 'or a DOAC' to the explanation so students are not taught DOACs are contraindicated.

7.concern: The age in the keyed option is wrong for the modality it names. Primary HPV testing is NOT endorsed from age 21 — ACS starts primary HPV at 25, USPSTF (2018) permits hrHPV-alone only from 30 (cytology alone 21-29). 'Primary HPV testing every 5 years, generally starting at age 21-25' conflates the start age for cytology with the start age for HPV testing. The module has the same conflation, so the fix belongs in both. D is still the only correct option (all others are clearly wrong), but the stated age range should read 25 (or 25-30).

6.concern: Distractor D ('Empiric perioperative FLOT chemotherapy with no further staging at all') names the actual guideline-standard treatment for resectable gastric cancer and is only made wrong by its trailing clause. A student who knows FLOT may pick D. Reword D to remove the correct-therapy bait (e.g. 'Proceed straight to gastrectomy with no further staging').
